Daily Quiz.question: ১) ‘Mosca’ is a character in -
Daily Quiz.exp:
‘Mosca’ is an important character in the play ‘Volpone’ by Ben Johnson.
Other important characters are: Volpone, Celia, Bonario, Corvino, Voltore.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action is called ballad. Ballad is mainly of two types: 1) The Folk and 2) The Literary Ballad.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) ‘Ignorance is not innocence but sin’ is written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Ignorance is not innocence but sin.
- The Inn Album.
- Robert Browning
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) An implicit or indirect reference to another work of literature is called -
Daily Quiz.exp:
An implicit or indirect reference to another work of literature, a historical or mythical person or event.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question:
৫) ‘Eternal passion!
Eternal pain!’ is a quote from -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Listen, Eugenia—
How thick the bursts come crowding through the leaves!
Again—thou hearest?
Eternal passion!
Eternal pain!
- Matthew Arnold 
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture and Poetryfoundation

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) The character ‘Robinson Crusoe’ is found in which writer’s writing?
Daily Quiz.exp:
‘Robinson Crusoe’, novel by Daniel Defoe, first published in London in 1719. Defoe’s first long work of fiction, it introduced two of the most-enduring characters in English literature: Robinson Crusoe and Friday.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) ''To Mercy pity peace and loves, All Pray in Their Distress''- is a quote taken from-
Daily Quiz.exp:
To Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
All pray in their distress;
And to these virtues of delight
Return their thankfulness.

For Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is God, our father dear,
And Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is Man, his child and care.

-The Divine Image
By - WILLIAM BLAKE

The Divine Image is part of Songs of Innocence.
Songs of Innocence was first published in 1789 followed by the publication of Songs of Experience in 1794. William Blake mostly wrote romantic poetry and prophetic works.
The Divine Image portrays an ideal world. The poem presents four traditional Christian virtues (Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love), which exist in the human heart and connect it with God.

Daily Quiz.question:
৮) 'The fair breeze blew, the white foam flew,
The furrow followed free' is an example of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Repetition of consonant sounds at the beginning of words or stressed syllables is known as alliteration.
Example: “Puffs, powders, patches, Bibles, billet-doux''. (Pope: The Rape of the Lock)
Here, ''p'' and ''b'' have been repeated.
Another example: The fair breeze blew, the white foam flew,
The furrow followed free;
(Coleridge: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner)
Here, ''f'' and ''b'' have been repeated.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) ‘Jane Bennet’ is a character of-
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) A pair of Blue Eyes
Daily Quiz.exp:
'Pride and Prejudice' is a famous Novel of Jane Austen. Important characters of 'Pride and Prejudice' are Mrs Darcy, Elizabeth Bennet, Jane Bennet.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) “Ten thousand saw I at a glance” is an example of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Hyperbole is an exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement. Here “Ten thousand saw I at a glance” - is an example of hyperbole. It used to create strong emotional responses.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Main literary features of the Old English Period are -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Heroic deeds, love of Sea adventures, intense love of glory and savage are the main literary features of Old English period.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Which one is the golden age of English Literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Elizabethan Period is called the golden English Literary period.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) A lyric poem mourning for death is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
A lyric poem mourning for death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event is called elegy. Gray’s “Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard”, Tennyson’s “In Memoriam” are two of the best elegies in English literature.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Which is the period of ''original romanticism''?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Elizabethan Age (1558 – 1603):
Features:
- ইংল্যান্ডের রাণী Queen Elizabeth এর নামানুসারে নামকরণ।
- এটি Golden Age হিসাবে পরিচিত।
- This period is a period of original romanticism.
- This period was replete with lyrics and songs.
- The literature shows a quest for ‘The remote, the wonderful and beautiful’.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Comparison between two different things is called -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Comparison between two different things is called metaphor.
It is a compressed form of simile.
''Liza is a rose'' is an example of metaphor as there is an implied comparison between the colour, softness, fragrance, beauty etc. of the rose and those of Liza.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica]

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) In which period Revival of Romanticism took place?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Romantic Period started in 1798 with William Wordswoth's ''Lyrical Ballads''. Revival of Romanticism took place in the Romantic Period. Lyrical Ballads brought about a great change in literature, both in subject and style.
source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) The comparison of unlike things using the words like or as is known to be-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Simile is an explicit comparison between two unlike entities. In the simile, unlike the metaphor, the resemblance is explicitly indicated by the words “like” or “as”. Example: My affection hath unknown bottom, like the Bay of Portugal.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) The character 'Yahoo' is found in the fiction-
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) The War of the Worlds
Daily Quiz.exp:
Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver’s Travel (fiction).
Characters of this book are: Gulliver, Blefuscudian, Yahoos, Houyhnhnms, Lilliputians, Laputans.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Catherine Earnshaw is a character from-
Daily Quiz.option3: গ) The Cry of the Children
Daily Quiz.exp:
Emily Bronte wrote Wuthering Heights. Its characters are: Catherine Earnshaw, Cathy Linton, Edgar Linton, Heathcliff, Lockwood.
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) A work which has a meaning behind the surface meaning is a/an -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Allegory is a literary form in which one story is told in the guise of another story.
In other words, an allegory is a story of double meanings.
Allegory, a symbolic fictional narrative that conveys a meaning not explicitly set forth in the narrative.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica]

Daily Quiz.question: ২১) To be or not to be: that is the ______.
Daily Quiz.exp:
To be or not to be: that is the question (Uttered by Hamlet)
- Hamlet.
- William Shakespeare
Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ২২) 'Ophelia' is a character from William Shakespeare’s tragedy-
Daily Quiz.exp: Characters of William Shakespeare's tragedy ‘Hamlet’ are: Hamlet, Horatio, Ophelia, Claudius etc. Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২৩) Which time period is known as “Renaissance Period” in English literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Renaissance Age (1500 – 1660)
Literary Features: - Originated in Italy (Florence City).
- Renaissance spirit was the main force that characterized the literature of this age.
- Major Features à l) Aestheticism. ll) Humanism. lll) Nationalism. lV) Spirit of Adventure.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৪) 'King Duncan' is a character in-
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) A Woman of No Importance
Daily Quiz.exp:
King Duncan, Macbeth, Macduff are the important characters of Shakespeare's play ‘Macbeth’. Macbeth was beheaded by Macduff.
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২৫) So farewell Hope, and with Hope farewell ____.
Daily Quiz.exp:
So farewell Hope, and with Hope farewell Fear,
Farewell Remorse: all Good to me is lost;
Evil be thou my Good.
John Milton: Paradise Lost
Source: Britannica

Daily Quiz.question: ২৬) Which is a form of lyric?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Lyric: A short poem expressing personal or subjunctive thoughts and intense feelings of a single speaker.
The sonnet, ode, elegy, hymn, dramatic monologue, epithalamion are the different forms of lyric.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৭) Which age is not in the Renaissance Period?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Renaissance period is divided into Elizabethan, Jacobean, Caroline and Commonwealth Period. Barren age is a part of The Middle English Period.
source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ২৮) A comedy which portrays the ridiculous behaviour pattern of the individuals of an aristocratic society is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
A comedy which portrays the ridiculous behaviour pattern of the individuals of an aristocratic society is called Comedy of Manners. It traditionally focuses on the infidelity, intrigue, immorality, jealousy, coarseness etc. of an artificial society.
The Way of the World by Congreve and The School for Scandal by Sheridan are examples of it.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৯) The period from AD 1066 to 1500 is known as -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The time frame AD 1066 to 1500 is known as 'The Middle English Period'.
It has three parts:
1. The Anglo-Norman Period
2. Age of Chaucer
3. Barren Age
Source: Live MCQ lecture

Daily Quiz.question: ৩০) “All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand” is a quotation from -
Daily Quiz.exp:
‘All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand’ হলো William Shakespeare রচিত Macbeth ট্রাজেডিতে Lady Macbeth এর একটি বিখ্যাত উক্তি।
Source: Live MCQ Lecture
